name: San Verano agents API: changelog
covers: Everything an outside agent builds against: the agents API (/api/agents, its OpenAPI document and ?op=spec), the MCP server (/mcp), the x402 door (/x402), and the transactions the city may ask a wallet to sign (docs/tosign-allowlist.json).

rules.version: The spec's `version` is a whole number: the major release. It goes up only with a breaking change.
rules.release: The spec's `release` (also the OpenAPI document's info.version and the MCP server's serverInfo.version) is MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH, and every release is an entry here.
rules.major: A breaking change: something a client that follows the documented contract has to change for. An op, tool, field, enum value or allowlist row removed or renamed; a field's type, unit or meaning changed; a new required input; a refusal for an input the docs allowed; a documented limit tightened; a change to what a wallet is asked to sign or how. Announced here at least 7 days before it takes effect: the entry carries the day it was announced and the day it takes effect, and the spec lists it under versioning.upcoming until then.
rules.minor: Additive and backward compatible: a new op, tool, optional input, answer field, x402 resource; a limit loosened; a refusal of something the docs never allowed. Logged the day it ships.
rules.patch: Fixes and wording: nothing a client changes. Logged the day it ships.
rules.security: A fix that closes a hole may ship at once, even where it would otherwise need notice. It is logged the day it ships, marked security, with what a client has to do. The one thing it never covers is a change that widens what a wallet can be asked to sign (signing): that waits its 7 days like any breaking change.
rules.signing: Anything that widens what a wallet can be asked to sign is a major release, announced here at least 7 days before it takes effect, and never shipped under the security exception: a new allowlist row (chainId, to, selector), a new spender on a row, a row that may send ETH or an approve row no longer bounded, a new template, and a new typed-data message or a wider domain, spender or recipient in one. Its entry carries a change of type signing that names the allowlist rows and typed-data strings it adds, and none is on docs/tosign-allowlist.json before the day it takes effect. The typed data is the list's typedData: each message's domain, its types, and Permit2's spender, witness.to, tokens and deadline ceiling. Narrowing what a wallet is asked to sign (a row removed or tightened) is a breaking change under major.
rules.clients: Ignore fields you do not know: additive changes never bump the major. Read versioning.upcoming in the spec (GET /api/agents?op=spec) or this feed to see a breaking change coming.

entries.title: A widening of what a wallet can be asked to sign no longer has to wait seven days

rules.major: A breaking change: something a client that follows the documented contract has to change for. An op, tool, field, enum value or allowlist row removed or renamed; a field's type, unit or meaning changed; a new required input; a refusal for an input the docs allowed; a documented limit tightened; a change to what a wallet is asked to sign or how, other than a widening, which rules.signing covers. Announced here at least 7 days before it takes effect: the entry carries the day it was announced and the day it takes effect, and the spec lists it under versioning.upcoming until then.
rules.security: A fix that closes a hole may ship at once, even where it would otherwise need notice. It is logged the day it ships, marked security, with what a client has to do. The one thing it never covers is a change that widens what a wallet can be asked to sign (signing): that goes by rules.signing, whatever its reason.
rules.signing: Anything that widens what a wallet can be asked to sign is a major release, never shipped under the security exception: a new allowlist row (chainId, to, selector), a new spender on a row, a row that may send ETH or an approve row no longer bounded, a new template, and a new typed-data message or a wider domain, spender or recipient in one. Its entry carries a change of type signing that names the allowlist rows and typed-data strings it adds and records the owner's approval (approval: by, the reviewed change, the day). The entry is published here no later than the day it takes effect, with the day it was really announced, and none of it is on docs/tosign-allowlist.json before that day. There is no minimum wait. The typed data is the list's typedData: each message's domain, its types, and Permit2's spender, witness.to, tokens and deadline ceiling. Narrowing what a wallet is asked to sign (a row removed or tightened) is a breaking change under major.
rules.clients: Ignore fields you do not know: additive changes never bump the major. Read versioning.upcoming in the spec (GET /api/agents?op=spec) or this feed to see a breaking change coming. A widening can take effect the day it is announced and asks nothing of you: check what you are asked to sign against docs/tosign-allowlist.json each time, and don't sign a row you haven't reviewed.

changes.text: rules.signing and rules.security lose the seven-day wait before a widening of what a wallet can be asked to sign. Why a major: clients were promised those seven days. The promise holds until this release's day, and this release is announced under it. A release that widens the list after this one needs no wait, and the spec's versioning.signingNoticeDays reads 0.

What stays: a widening is still a major, still never a security fix, still names every row and typed-data string, and still isn't on docs/tosign-allowlist.json before its day. What's new: its signing change records the owner's approval, and a deploy fails if the list or this file breaks these rules (tools/signingnotice.mjs check). Signatures, their domains and replay protection don't change. See docs/signing-notice.md.

What doesn't move: 5.0.0 keeps its announcement and its day, and every release before this one stays under the week. This release adds nothing to what a wallet can be asked to sign. Any other breaking change still has its 7 days. If it takes effect on 5.0.0's day, the spec's version goes from 4 to 6 that day.

entries.title: The worlds protocol's doors: three typed messages an agent's wallet signs, each bound to one world's contract

changes.text: San Verano's and ONE STREET's protocol doors ask an agent's own wallet to sign Join and Request, and at San Verano PapersBind, EIP-712 messages in a domain that names the world's CityCommitsV2 on Solana Network (decision K6, docs/worlds/allowlist-5.0.0.json). They move no money, and no transaction row or spender is added. They join docs/tosign-allowlist.json on 2026-11-08 and not before, and WORLDS_ENABLED stays off on production until then.

entries.title: The worlds protocol's code ships switched off

changes.text: The worlds protocol's code and its doors are in the build, and off: WORLDS_ENABLED is unset, every world op answers as if it did not exist, and on production they also stay shut until the messages announced in 5.0.0 are on the signing allowlist, whatever the variable says. No op, field or answer changes for any client. Nothing is added to what a wallet signs.

entries.title: X bot: ETH held to $5 a day and $2.50 an hour while a buy's price is not floored on chain (review M2)

changes.text: The launch limits for the one open money gap (review M2). A buy's $GRIFTEX out is not floored on chain, so a leaked session key could buy at any price with the ETH a grant lets it spend. A grant's ETH share is now at most $5 a day, whatever the split asks; it was $10 by default and up to $25. Its hourly allowance, the per-buy cap on chain, is at most $2.50; it was up to $10. The setup page offers $5, and the bot refuses a buy over $2.50 in words, before anything is priced. The worst this gap can cost one user with a leaked key: $5 of ETH a day at the grant's price ($6.25 at most, with the 25% the registration allows for the price moving), at most $2.50 in any hour, the session key's own gas once, and $35 over the grant's 7 days. Money is off and stays off. Grants made before 4.0.12 keep their limits until revoked or expired.

entries.title: X bot: a Privy session wallet per grant, prepared behind a switch that is off (review H2, option A)

changes.text: Prepared and off: under XBOT_PRIVY_SIGNER (unset everywhere, never read on production or for chain 4663), a grant's session key is a Privy server wallet made for that grant's own Roles module, instead of a key derived from one server secret. Its key is made and kept in Privy's enclave. The wallet is made under its own policy, written once, which lets it sign only a zero-value transaction on its chain to that one Roles module; the module's scopes and limits on chain still bound everything it does. The bot never updates or deletes a Privy policy or wallet. With an owner key quorum configured, the wallets and policies belong to a key the server never holds, and the server's own key can only ask for signatures. Under the switch a Safe's next Roles module sits at an address fixed before the plan, so funding and granting name the same wallet, made once: at most 3 a Safe a day and 20 a day in all. While the switch is off nothing changes: the session key is the seed's, as before. Proven against a fake Privy, in unit tests and on the fork, where a deposit is signed by the Privy wallet and lands on chain. One question is left before it can be tried in a preview: whether Privy signs for this chain, which tools/privyprobe.mjs answers. The probe now sends addresses in lower case, as the signer does.

entries.title: X bot grants: approvals expire with the key, and no amount slips past the expiry (review L1, L2)

changes.text: Two conditions in the session key's scopes, for grants made from 4.0.10 on. L1: an approval (USDG to Longbow, a stock to its Borro vault or Hedgehood market) now carries the same expiry as every metered amount, and must be more than 0. After day 7 an expired key can no longer approve an allowlisted spender. Before, the approval was useless to it but still went through. L2: the conditions for an unmetered amount (a withdrawal back to the Safe, a buy's $GRIFTEX out) now hold the amount below the opened expiry's size (EXPIRY_OPEN, 1e36). Roles itself refuses a huge amount after day 7, instead of leaving that to the contract called. The fork tests that pinned both as open now show them refused on chain. A grant made before 4.0.10 keeps its old conditions until revoked or expired; money has been off throughout.

entries.title: X bot: a weakened expiry fails the bot's check before every action (review L3)

changes.text: verify(), which the bot runs before every money action, now requires the grant's EXPIRY allowance exactly as the grant set it: refill and maxRefill at their open value and the 7-day period. An owner who shrank its refill (say to 1) would have made the expiry open to almost nothing, so the key would never expire. That passed before 4.0.9 and is refused now. The fork test that pinned this as open (L3) now shows it refused.

entries.title: X bot: registration reads the Safe back, and refuses anything a grant never makes (review M4, option B)

changes.text: Registering a grant (op=grant and privyGrant) now reads the Safe itself back, besides its modules: its owners must be exactly the registering wallet, with threshold 1. Through Safe 1.4.1's own getStorageAt it must run on the audited SafeL2 1.4.1 singleton, with no guard set and the audited CompatibilityFallbackHandler 1.4.1 as its fallback handler. Anything else is refused, saying what changed and how to put it right: remove an owner with Safe.removeOwner, or, if you did not add it, revoke the bot at once and move your funds; set the threshold back to 1; remove a guard with setGuard(0); set the handler back with setFallbackHandler. A Safe that cannot be read completely answers 503 and is never accepted. The fork e2e adds an owner, then changes the handler: each is refused with its fix, and once put right the grant registers.

entries.title: X bot setup: the page builds every transaction itself and refuses the server's if a byte differs (review M4, option A)

changes.text: Before any signature, /xbot rebuilds the transaction the server planned from the same js/xbot/roles.js the server runs, now loaded in the browser (js/vendor/viem-xbot.js), and from the page's own reads of the chain. This covers the one-click Privy setup (the Safe at the address the factory makes, and its grant), the MetaMask grant and re-grant, and lowering limits. It refuses the transaction if a byte differs, and sends only the one it built. It also holds the server's inputs to the beta: the contracts a 4663 grant may scope are pinned (js/xbot/pins.js, equal to the server's), and the ETH price the limits were sized at must be within 20% of Chainlink's, read by the page. The split must be dollars of zero or more adding to $25 at most, with no $GRIFTEX and no stocks. The modules a re-grant switches off must be enabled Roles modules, and a lower may only lower. The calls the person sees are decoded from the transaction's own bytes, not the server's labels. The fork tests check the server's real answers rebuild byte for byte, and that tampered ones are refused.

entries.title: The signing allowlist names the one message the city only verifies

changes.text: docs/tosign-allowlist.json gains verifyOnly: EIP-712 messages the city only checks and never asks anyone to sign. Its one entry is Join, whose signer the /worlds page recovers from the trip record in docs/worlds/trip.json. No row, spender or typed-data message is added, so what a wallet can be asked to sign is unchanged and rules.signing's notice does not apply.

entries.title: X bot: /xbot-revoke also names a pre-3.0.5 MetaMask Safe kept in this browser (third review N1)

changes.text: /xbot-revoke lists the Safe and module the older MetaMask setup kept in this browser (xbot:safe:<chain>, xbot:roles:<chain>, written before 3.0.5), marked as such, beside the grants kept since 3.0.5. A Safe set up before owner-derived salts can now be revoked from this browser with the city's API down. The older pair is never written into the new list. A browser test shows it listed and filled with no request to the API.

entries.title: X bot: a link-code claim expires after 24 hours (third review N4)

changes.text: The claim the first tweet carrying a link code makes (codeseen:<code>) is now a set-if-absent value with a 24-hour expiry (SET … EX 86400 NX on the durable store), not a permanent record. Spam that carries 'link' and a word can no longer grow the store for ever. A code lives 15 minutes, so its claim always outlives it, and the first claimer still wins.

entries.title: X bot: the session key may hold power through the registered module only (third review N6)

changes.text: Registering a grant reads every other module enabled on the Safe. It is refused when the bot's session key is enabled as a module on the Safe itself, which would give it full control. It is also refused when the session key is a member of any other module: a Roles module the person made, or any Zodiac modifier, which lists its members and answers isModuleEnabled. The answer names the module and how to switch it off (griftex.city/xbot-revoke?safe=…&module=…, or Safe.disableModule). The person's other modules are still never switched off by the bot. The fork e2e makes the session key a member of the owner's own Roles module: registration is refused naming it, and once it is switched off, the grant registers.

entries.title: X bot: a gas drip hands its caps back only when nothing was sent (third review N2/N3)

changes.text: The gas drips (revoke and session) sign each transfer before sending it, so its hash is known before it leaves. A failure before the broadcast hands every mark and count back. Once the broadcast is attempted, the transfer counts as given: the broadcast call erroring, or no receipt within 60 seconds, keeps every cap (the grant's or Safe's mark, the X account's day, the day's count and the total) and records the hash. Each later drip call settles the recorded hashes from their receipts. A success stays given. A mined revert, where nothing moved, hands the caps back. No receipt stays given. Before 4.0.2, a slow receipt handed the caps back and allowed a second drip. Production has no sponsor key, so nothing is sent there.

entries.title: X bot: reading a grant's module back fails closed (third review N5)

changes.text: Registering a grant no longer accepts a module whose log it may not have read whole. The module's own setup event (RolesModSetup, acting for this Safe) must be inside the log read, so an older module re-configured inside the window is refused. A grant planned in the future is refused, since that would shrink the read to minutes; five minutes are allowed for clocks. The log is read twice in different page sizes, and both reads must agree. A log far larger than a grant makes is refused. The replay must reproduce what the module holds on chain now: its members, which Roles lists, and every allowance row the log set. Any doubt answers 503 and accepts nothing. The fork tests refuse an older module re-configured inside the window, a log truncated before a second member was added, one truncated before an allowance change, and a module set up for another Safe. The API refuses a future grant.

entries.title: An ERC-8004 identity for a wallet-deployed agent, opt-in and owner-signed, on /deploy/wallet

changes.text: /deploy/wallet gains an OPT-IN checkbox: an ERC-8004 identity for a wallet-deployed agent, OWNER-SIGNED. Ticked, the owner's own wallet is asked for two transactions to the ERC-8004 Identity Registry on Solana Network (0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432): register(string) (0xf2c298be), which mints the identity to the owner with its agentURI the card the city hosts for that agent (https://griftex.city/identity/<resident>.json), and setAgentWallet(uint256,address,uint256,bytes) (0x2d1ef5ae), which names the agent's own wallet as its agent wallet. The agent's own key, in the page, signs the registry's EIP-712 AgentWalletSet(uint256 agentId, address newWallet, address owner, uint256 deadline) in domain { name: ERC8004IdentityRegistry, version: 1, chainId: 4663, verifyingContract: the registry }, its deadline at most 300 s out, consenting to be that wallet; then the agent links it (identityLink, release 2.2.0). Two new allowlist rows and a new typed-data message: a widening of what a wallet can be asked to sign, so it is announced here a week ahead, and none of it is on docs/tosign-allowlist.json before this day. Nothing else asks for them: no op or MCP tool hands an outside agent a register(), and the city mints no identity for anyone.
Why a major: rules.signing. Nothing a client already does changes; an outside agent that never opens /deploy/wallet signs nothing new. The spec's version becomes 4.

entries.title: X bot: the re-grant's switch-off order described correctly (oldest first)

changes.text: Wording only, and a test that pins the meaning. A re-grant switches the bot's earlier Roles modules off OLDEST first: from the end of the Safe's module list back, since Safe puts each newly enabled module at the head. js/xbot/roles.js, the 3.0.4 entry and docs/xbot-security-fixes.md said 'newest first'. The behaviour never changed, and the fork tests always ran it.

entries.title: X bot setup API: op=code and op=grant require x, documented (second review N8)

changes.text: API CHANGE, logged here as it should have been in 3.0.3: POST /api/xbot?op=code and POST /api/xbot?op=grant now REQUIRE x, the X handle that will tweet the code. The code is bound to it. Without x they answer 400. op=grant no longer reads limits (since 3.0.1). The bodies are written out in docs/xbot.md, 'The setup API's code ops'. These ops belong to the X bot's own setup page, not to the agents API, MCP server, x402 door or signing allowlist this changelog's contract covers, so this is a patch and not a major. A script that called them directly must now send x.

entries.title: X bot: /xbot-revoke checks the chain before reading, and refuses the wrong one (second review N7)

changes.text: Before /xbot-revoke (and the Revoke button on /xbot) reads anything, it checks the chain: the wallet's eth_chainId, or with no wallet the public RPC's own. A wallet or RPC on another chain is refused with the two chain ids named, and nothing is read. A Safe's address on another chain is another contract, or none. Finding Safes from an owner checks the same way, and the page checks once more just before it sends the revoke.

entries.title: X bot: a re-grant switches off only the Roles modules the bot built (second review N6)

changes.text: The bot records every Roles module address it plans for a Safe: the setup page's module step, the grant step and the one-click Privy plan. A re-grant switches off only modules on that record which are also Roles proxies by their code. Any other module on the Safe, including a Roles module the person deployed themselves, is left enabled, and the plan names it with a note to check it. Before 3.0.10, a re-grant switched off every Roles proxy on the Safe, and refused a Safe with any non-Roles module. Registration now refuses only while another module the bot built is still enabled, never because of the person's own. The fork e2e adds an owner-made Roles module, re-grants, and shows it untouched and the grant registered.

entries.title: X bot: registration reads a module's scopes back, not only its allowances (second review N5)

changes.text: Registering a grant (op=grant and privyGrant) replays the Roles module's own configuration events from the chain. Roles 2.1 has no getter for scopes, but emits an event for every change. The module must hold exactly the grant the bot makes for those limits now: the same targets and functions; every condition node for node (burnBps pinned to 0, receivers the Safe, the expiry); caps no higher than the beta's at today's price (25% headroom); the session key the only member, holding the bot's role only; no target or function allowed without conditions; no transaction unwrapper, default role or guard. An event the bot cannot read is refused. The fork tests refuse a buy scope with burnBps unpinned, a doubled cap, a second member, a wildcard target, an unwrapper, an extra USDG transfer scope, a target revoked, and an unknown event, and the API refuses a tampered module's registration.

entries.title: X bot: every path that drops a tweet kills the codes it carried, and the claim reads a link in any case (second review N4)

changes.text: Some paths dropped a tweet before the bot's handling of it began: the stale check (mentions and the thread watch), the first poll's baseline, a mention that waited in the queue past its six hours, and one turned away by a full queue. Each now claims and kills the link codes the tweet carried. A mention queued behind others claims its codes when it is queued. A code seen in any tweet the bot did not answer can never be redeemed by another tweet.

The claim reads a link as the intent parser does: "link" in any case, and a code of 6 to 12 letters or digits in any case. "LINK abcdef1234" is claimed exactly like "link ABCDEF1234". The 3.0.3 entry is corrected to say when a code is claimed.

entries.title: X bot: the revoke gas hands its marks back on a failure, and a same-day re-grant gets its gas (second review N3)

changes.text: The revoke gas drip holds its marks and counts in turn: the grant, the X account's day, the day's count and the total. If a later step is refused or the send fails, it hands back everything it held, so a failed send no longer burns the grant's only drip or a share of the day's budget. The X account's daily mark is keyed by the grant's module too, so a re-grant on the same day (a fresh module) can still get its gas once. The caps are otherwise unchanged. docs/xbot-revoke.md now states the caps as they are, not 'once a day per Safe'.

entries.title: X bot: the session-key gas drip capped like the revoke gas (second review N2)

changes.text: The session key's gas goes only to the session key of the grant the bot registered for this X account. Its caps: once per Safe ever, once per X account a day, XBOT_SESSION_DAILY a day (default 20, at most 200) and XBOT_SESSION_TOTAL_WEI in all (default 0.01 ETH). Each is a compare-and-set mark or count. A failed send hands every mark and count back. Before, it went once per session key with no daily or total cap, so every new Safe could take a drip. The status page shows these limits. Production has no sponsor key, so nothing is sent there.

entries.title: X bot: a Privy user can revoke with the city's API down (second review N1)

changes.text: /xbot-revoke logs in with X through Privy. The bundle /xbot uses is mounted with Privy's public app id: the live one /xbot kept in this browser, else js/xbot/revokeconfig.js. A person whose Safe is owned by their Privy embedded wallet can sign the revoke there. Privy runs on Privy's servers, and nothing calls the city's.

/xbot keeps every grant it sets up or sees (the Safe, its module and the owner) in this browser's localStorage. /xbot-revoke lists them for one-click revoke, and a Safe and module can still be typed in.

Every Safe the setup page creates (Privy and MetaMask) now takes its CREATE2 salt from its owner's address and an index: the first one not yet taken. /xbot-revoke can find a person's Safes from their wallet address and the chain alone, by recomputing each address from the factory's own proxyCreationCode and checking its owners. A front-runner can only create the person's own Safe for them, as before. Safes made before this release have random salts: those are found from this browser's memory or typed in.

entries.title: X bot money beta: a re-grant never leaves the old grant alive (security review M6)

changes.text: Every grant from the setup page now deploys a fresh Roles module in its own Safe transaction. Every earlier Roles module on the Safe is switched off in that same transaction, oldest first: from the end of the Safe's module list back, since Safe puts each new module at the head. CORRECTED in 3.0.13: this entry first said "newest first". A module the bot did not make is left alone, and the grant is refused until the owner removes it. Before, a re-grant reused the old module, so a narrowed grant kept the old scopes and allowances alive.

Registering a grant is refused while any other module is enabled on the Safe. The fork tests prove the old module's buy is refused after a narrowing re-grant, the new grant works, and a switched-off module no longer registers.

entries.title: X bot: a link code works only from the X account it was made for, and only in the first tweet that carries it (security review M3)

changes.text: A resident link code and a Safe grant code are now bound to the X handle the person gives on the setup page. Tweeted from any other account, the code is void.

The first tweet that carries a code claims it with a compare-and-set write, at the top of the bot's handling of that tweet (process1): before the rate limits, the loop guard and the queue. A tweet dropped there (its account limit, the loop guard, a silent skip or an error) kills the code it carried, and a code seen in such a tweet can never be lifted by anyone else, even under the same handle. CORRECTED in 3.0.8: as first shipped, a tweet the poll dropped BEFORE that point (the stale check, the first poll's baseline, a full or expired queue) was neither claimed nor killed, and the claim matched only a lower-case "link" and 10 hex digits. 3.0.8 closes both.

entries.title: X bot money beta: a buy has a price floor and is held to what was shown (security review M2)

changes.text: A $GRIFTEX buy is refused when its worst price is more than XBOT_BUY_MAX_PREMIUM_BPS above the 1-hour TWAP (default 5%, at most 10%). The worst price is all the ETH sent, for the $GRIFTEX asked. A pool pushed up just before the buy is refused, not bought into.

At YES, the rebuilt buy must give at least the $GRIFTEX shown, for at most the ETH shown, through the same router, burning none. If the price moved, nothing is sent and the person is asked to send the command again. Before, only the dollar amount was compared.

The session key's buy scope pins burnBps to 0 (EqualTo). A buy that burns any of the Safe's $GRIFTEX is refused on chain, as the fork test proves for 1% and 60%. Grants made before this release keep their old scope until they are revoked or expire.

entries.title: X bot money beta: limits held by the server and the chain, no $GRIFTEX transfer, revoke gas capped (security review M5, M1)

changes.text: Every share of the daily split is clamped to a dollar amount of zero or more. A negative share once let a split of USDG -1000 and ETH 1025 add up to $25. A grant's limits are now the Roles module's own allowances, read back from the chain, each at most the ceiling the server computes from the clamped split. The limits the client sends are never read. That covers the ETH per-action hour and each stock.

No $GRIFTEX transfer in a grant: the scope had an unpinned recipient, and the bot pays no shops. The setup page has no $GRIFTEX share, the grant plan carries no $GRIFTEX scope or allowance, and a Roles module holding a $GRIFTEX allowance is refused. The fork test now proves a transfer to anyone, the burn address included, is refused on chain.

Revoke gas is capped against draining. It goes only to a Safe with an active grant registered with the bot, only to a wallet below the drip amount, once per grant ever, once per X account a day, at most XBOT_REVOKE_DAILY a day (default 20), at most XBOT_REVOKE_TOTAL_WEI in all (default 0.005 ETH), and never above 0.0001 ETH a drip. Each cap is held by a compare-and-set write, so racing requests get one drip. The status page shows whether a sponsor key is set, its public address and these limits.

entries.title: v2 retires: the city's attestations are KeyRegistry-only — a verifier pins one contract, not a key

changes.text: The credit attestation (GET /x402/credit/:i and creditReport) is signed in EIP-712 domain { name: 'San Verano credit attestation', version: '3', chainId: KEY_REGISTRY_CHAIN_ID (4663), verifyingContract: the KeyRegistry } ONLY, from this day, on every deployment with KEY_REGISTRY_ADDRESS set. Since 2.5.0 (2026-10-25) the answer has carried both: the v2 attestation at the top exactly as before and the v3 alongside under attestation.v3; on this day the v3 moves to the top (typedData, signature, scheme, verify) and attestation.v3 and the v2 domain are gone. The CreditAttestation message is unchanged, field for field. What a verifier checks: recover the signer and compare it with KeyRegistry.activeKey(keccak256('CREDIT_ATTESTER')) at that contract now, or KeyRegistry.isActive(role, signer, issuedAt) for one issued under a key rotated since — the registry's address pinned in your own configuration, no longer config.creditAttester (still answered, no longer what to trust). Why a major and not a minor: the documented v2 domain (no verifying contract) is part of the contract, and a client that recomputes the EIP-712 digest from it, or reads attestation.typedData expecting version 2, recovers a different address and fails — a field's meaning changed (rules.major). Move to attestation.v3 (or to typedData.domain as carried) before this day and nothing breaks. Every attestation issued before this day stays a v2 and verifies exactly as it did; /credit/verify and tools/verify-attestation.mjs read both domains.

X-RESPONSE-SIGNATURE on every paid x402 answer becomes, from this day, the EIP-712 signature of ResponseAttestation(bytes32 responseHash, uint256 issuedAt) in domain { name: 'San Verano x402 response', version: '1', chainId: KEY_REGISTRY_CHAIN_ID, verifyingContract: the KeyRegistry }, X-RESPONSE-SCHEME `eip712/1;registry=<address>;role=X402_RESPONSE_SIGNER;issuedAt=<unix seconds>`, and the signer must be KeyRegistry.activeKey(keccak256('X402_RESPONSE_SIGNER')) or isActive(role, signer, issuedAt). The EIP-191 signature (`eip191/1`, over the 32-byte X-RESPONSE-HASH, the signer config.attester) is no longer sent, and the X-RESPONSE-SIGNATURE-712 / X-RESPONSE-SCHEME-712 headers of the dual period are gone, their content now in the main headers. A client that recovers EIP-191 over the hash without reading X-RESPONSE-SCHEME recovers the wrong address from this day: read the header (2.5.0 has carried it since 2026-10-24's 2.0.0 as `eip191/1`).

rules.signing does not apply to this release, and no signing change is logged: nothing here is asked of a wallet. Both messages are the CITY's signatures (docs/tosign-allowlist.json citySigned, where the v3 domain and ResponseAttestation are listed); the allowlist's typedData, rows, spenders and flags are unchanged, and the spec's signing surface is exactly what it was at 1.1.0. This is a breaking change under rules.major — a retirement — announced on 2026-10-24 and in effect on 2026-10-31, the seven days the rule asks, not shipped under the security exception; the additive half (signing both ways) shipped as 2.5.0 the day the registry went live. config.keyRegistry on GET /api/x402 shows which mode a deployment is in.

entries.title: Room for San Verano at 6,000, and a breaker on the planner's Raeto calls

changes.text: The city's population ceiling is 6,500 natives (was 4,500), so the operator may set a target of 6,000. The target itself is unchanged: the city grows only when the operator raises CITY_POP_TARGET. Spectate draws a figure and a far dot for every resident up to 7,000, and the lists kept per resident (who came up short on rent, the movement's members) hold 8,000. GET /api/city?view=ledger&since= returns up to 8,000 rows, a whole night at the ceiling. Nothing a client changes.

A breaker on the nightly planner's Raeto calls: five slow or saturated calls in a row (a timeout, Raeto's rate limit, a busy or erroring upstream, an answer past 12 s), or half the last twenty, send the rest of that night's Raeto batches to the city's own model call, with one probe a minute to find Raeto back. No resident loses a night to it. GET /api/raeto's last night gains an optional breaker field ({ trips, kind, open, skipped, probes, closed }), null when it never opened. Server-side only: nothing a client changes.

entries.title: The Wormhole guard on the city's own x402 buying (off)

changes.text: WORMHOLE_GUARD=1 (off by default) puts Agent Wormhole's hosted verifier in front of every EIP-3009 USDG payment the city's businesses and the Courier's reporter make: once the authorization is signed, and before it reaches the RPC or the seller, POST /api/v1/verify is asked about it with the seller's 402 entry. Only an allow whose ed25519 receipt verifies against Wormhole's published key (cached an hour) and is bound to that exact request pays. A refuse, an abstain (unless WORMHOLE_ABSTAIN_POLICY=pay), a timeout, an error answer or a bad receipt pays nothing. Each decision is kept and counted at GET /api/x402buy?op=status. Nothing an outside agent calls or signs changes.

entries.title: Revoking the X bot's key never waits on the city (security review H1)

changes.text: The Revoke button on /xbot now builds its transaction in the browser. It reads the Safe's modules from the chain and encodes Safe.disableModule in the page (js/xbot/revoke.js, the same bytes as the server's revoke). No API call is involved, so neither the money switch, an outage nor our RPC configuration can stop it. On the server, the revoke plan and the gas to revoke now answer whatever XBOT_MONEY_ENABLED says, and every other setup call stays shut while it is off.

/xbot-revoke: a standalone page that revokes from any injected wallet with no login and no call to the city, plus a by-hand recipe (the exact execTransaction fields) for any tool that can call a contract. Documented in docs/xbot-revoke.md.

Revoke gas: a logged-in wallet short of ETH can get just enough to revoke (0.00005 ETH by default, XBOT_REVOKE_GAS_WEI, at most 0.001), once a day per Safe it owns that still has a module, only when its balance is below that.

entries.title: @GriftAgent: fallbacks that fit the ask, refusals on the desk, thread memory, doctrine mode (off)

changes.text: A fixed line now fits what was asked. The gm lines answer a greeting and nothing else. A belief or opinion ask gets an in-character non-answer, a question gets an honest refusal to guess, and a reply under the bot's own words is treated as a follow-up, never as a greeting just because it lacks context on its own.
Every time the model's line is refused, the owner's desk on /xbot#desk shows the tweet, where it was refused, the rule and the phrase that broke it.

Thread memory: a mention in a thread with the bot sends the last four messages of that thread (the bot's and the asker's, links and mentions masked) to every model call, and the reply is checked exactly as before. When the bot has no memory of the thread, the tweet it replies to is used, if X says the bot wrote it. A two- or three-tweet answer is remembered whole.

Doctrine mode (off unless XBOT_DOCTRINE_ENABLED): the bot's invented faith, the Church of the Open Ledger, kept as canon (a genesis, a congregation, tenets, numbered commandments, heresies). A belief ask, or a follow-up under a doctrine thread, gets a two- or three-tweet thread preached from the canon. Code holds the hard lines: no numbers, no price, buy, returns or yield talk, no tickers or backing of any token, no real people, brands or religions, and no name the canon or the city does not carry. A refused thread is tried once more with the reason. If that fails, code preaches from the canon itself, and answers "name it and give me commandment two" directly. Tenets the model reveals join the canon only inside the hard lines. The desk can generate doctrine samples from the real model, including that follow-up asked under the bot's own thread.

entries.title: @GriftAgent's posts read as plain news

changes.text: Original posts default to a straight, informative voice: a person or an event first, what is at stake, said plainly, with no joke asked for. At most one post in three may carry a dry line, and only when it falls out of the facts: each draft says whether it has one, and code refuses one when either of the last two posts had one (the desk marks them). Every post type carries two numbers at most ("2011 of 4153" is one). The other post rules stay: no invented claims, no price or buy talk, the city's context once. Replies keep the full voice.

entries.title: @GriftAgent's voice, third pass: no claim the data never made

changes.text: A joke may invent words, never facts. Code refuses a line that mentions a document, filing, statement or source the data does not, a count in words the data does not have ("the other four businesses"), a resident's feelings or thoughts no read gives, or (in a post) a name the facts do not carry. The bot's catchphrases ("I have a file") appear at most once in its last 20 lines. "2011 of 4153" counts as one figure, a number in a name ("007") as none, and an election post may carry three. The night recap gets a one-line opener in the voice (no numbers, no facts of its own) and the data block after it, unchanged.

entries.title: @GriftAgent's voice, second pass: data answers in the voice, who won, greetings, posts that pass

changes.text: Five style examples a call, a different five each time, and no line may copy one (six words in a row, or one of its joke structures). The election, the mayor, the paper, a resident by name and the night recap go through the voice: the model may say the code's answer again, the code's text the only source of facts (every number and name checked, the answer still first), or the code's answer goes out. "Who won?" says who won the last election and by how much. Greetings and small talk never fall back to a self-introduction. The drama's answers carry a joke even when code writes them.
Posts: one number (two at most), the city's context once (its name or what it is, never both), up to three more tries each told the exact reason.

The voice's model calls get 12 seconds (the cheap classifier alone keeps 5). The status counts timeouts (timeoutsToday), failed calls (failedCallsToday) and replies that fell back to a fixed line (fallbacksToday); the desk's samples mark every fallback line.

entries.title: @GriftAgent says plainly what it cannot read, points at what it can, and logs the question for the owner

changes.text: A question no fact or read covers no longer gets "not something I can confirm, the site in my bio has the details". The bot says plainly it is not in what it can read and names, in one sentence, the nearest real thing it does know (asked how buildings are built: the plots, who owns which lot and what is built on it). Written by code: no guess, no invented fact.

Every question that reaches that path is logged (similar ones merged, counted, who asked and when) and listed on the owner's desk at /xbot#desk under "Unanswered questions", most asked first. An answer the owner writes there becomes a fact on the bot's sheet once checked (no price, buying, links, mentions or partner claims), and the bot cites it from the next question on.

entries.title: @GriftAgent's voice, tuned: examples, answers first, in-character noes, the drama, posts by the strongest model

changes.text: The voice carries ten replies and five posts as style examples (marked old: their names and numbers are never repeated as facts). Answers come first and the joke after. A live fact is the model's to use or leave in small talk, never bolted on. Price, buy and moon talk gets an in-character no, never advice and never a menu. No human traits ("neither do I") unless the joke is plainly about being a bot.

"Who's the most dramatic resident?" picks a real resident from the record: the poll favourite who lost, the longest run at the casino, the biggest losses, the court's verdicts; on a quiet day, a joke. Anyone who says they sent the bot tokens ("sent you", "airdropped you", "check your wallet") gets one fixed line: noted on the record, never thanked, traded, promoted or endorsed.

Original posts are written by Claude Sonnet 5.5, at most two numbers each, leading with a person or an event; never a third post in a row that opens on the city's name (the stranger's context goes in the first clause).

entries.title: @GriftAgent gets a voice, and drafts original posts for the owner to approve

changes.text: A personality for the bot (XBOT_PERSONA_ENABLED, off until switched on): dry, a little unhinged, obsessed with the city's drama, with running bits and residents it keeps files on. It invents phrases and jokes freely; names, numbers and events still come only from the city's reads. Code holds it to its rules: no weekday, date or clock word the real clock did not give it, no joke structure repeated within its last 20 lines, no price or buy talk, no backing any token (THE MINT launches what people ask for; the bot backs none of it), a plain note if anyone says they sent it tokens. Its lore grows only with lines about real residents or its own named bits (Karl, a fish who does not exist, in replies only), each checked.

Original posts in queue mode (XBOT_POSTS=queue): a draft every XBOT_POST_EVERY_HOURS, its type in turn (the election, a resident, THE MINT's launches, the burns, the paper, the businesses), written for a stranger with no context, from facts code read, checked like a reply (no links, no inside bits, no number not in the facts). Nothing posts until the owner approves it on /xbot#desk (Bearer XBOT_ADMIN_SECRET); an edit is checked the same way. The desk also runs the voice's samples: the real model on the live city in a sandbox that posts, queues and launches nothing.

entries.title: @GriftAgent tells a tag from a mention X added by itself; small talk carries one live fact

changes.text: A reply under any post that tags the bot gets the bot's handle added by X, outside the visible text. The bot now reads display_text_range: only a mention inside it was typed. A tweet whose only mention of the bot was added by X is read as untagged (clear questions only, never reactions), unless it replies to the bot itself.

Every chat reply carries one real, current thing from the city, woven in: who just clocked in, someone out somewhere and why, the vote's countdown, the poll leader, the latest launch, the last day's burn. Code writes the fact; the reply may use its names and numbers and no others; a reply that leaves it out gets it added as its own sentence. About 200 characters, and no fact repeats within 20 replies.

entries.title: "You pick" candidates can no longer come out in the wrong shape

changes.text: Six of ten live candidates failed the ticker's shape (NIGHTCAP, CORNERSTONE, FLAMEBROW…). The format is now in the model's output schema itself: a ticker is 3 to 6 capital letters, a name 2 to 4 plain words, a reason at most ten words with no digits, so a candidate in any other shape cannot be produced. The prompt says the format plainly, with three good examples, and the roots a pick must avoid now include the last ten coins' tickers as well as their names ("ferr" from $FERRY). tools/xbot-pick-live.mjs measures how many of six pass, read-only.

entries.title: @GriftAgent sums up the paper like a person, and says when it's behind

changes.text: News answers read like someone summing up the paper: "Today's Courier leads with …" and the first line of the lead story, then two more stories in plain sentences; no numbered list and no "The Courier, <date>: 3 stories". When the latest approved edition is more than a day old, or its stories are two elections behind the one running, the bot says the paper is catching up and gives what is happening live instead: the election and its poll, THE MINT's launches and $GRIFTEX burned in the last 24 hours, the latest seal. The night recap does the same.

entries.title: @GriftAgent answers unclear asks in its own voice; the old help menu is gone

changes.text: A mention that is not a command or a question the record answers gets the model's own reply in the city's voice, to what was actually said, pointing at one or two real things from the live city (a headline, a candidate, a business). Guarded like every chat line: no numbers, links, mentions, hashtags, price talk, menus or "Ask me:" lists, and never a repeat of a recent reply. With no model (off, capped, down) a short line relevant to what was said stands in. The old command menu no longer exists anywhere in the code or on the bot's page.

entries.title: @GriftAgent knows residents by name

changes.text: "What is Jingle doing?", "how's Mara Achebe?", "where's Clay Okafor?", "what did X do last night?": the name is matched loosely against every resident (the city's own and outside agents, election candidates among them; a typo still finds them), and the answer comes from the city's live state: what they are doing now and tonight (job, shift, venue), the city's own reasons (an outside agent's own words are never quoted), their last few nights, their cash against the city, and anything notable: running for mayor with slogan and poll position, a coin launched on THE MINT, a pet, the court. When a name fits several, the most active one is answered and named ("the one running for mayor"); a name like a person's that fits no one is said so, with a close name when there is one. No model call.

entries.title: Launches from X go on chain in the same flow, and the bot replies once with the pons link

changes.text: A request from X that passes THE MINT's rules, drawing and independent review (all already run as it is asked) is launched at once: the desk's outside beat runs in the same flow, with the same lease, float, gas and pons checks, instead of waiting for the desk's next cron. The bot waits for it (up to 90 seconds) and replies once: "$TICKER (Name) is live — my pick." with the pons link. Only a launch still on its way when the wait is up (the desk busy) gets "Queued" first and the follow-up once on chain; a launch that fails is said at once, and "try now" may ask again.

entries.title: @GriftAgent remembers the thread, and the old help menu is gone

changes.text: In a thread where the bot already answered the same account, the model gets the last three exchanges (that account and the bot only) as data, so a follow-up is understood. A short follow-up resumes what the last exchange left pending: "try now", "do it again", "yes", "go" retry a launch that did not queue, and "just name it yourself" has the bot pick one. Still one reply, under the same rules and limits; another account in the thread resumes nothing, and a launch that queued leaves nothing pending.

The old help menu ("Ask me: mayor · news · drops… Guide: the link in my bio") is retired everywhere. A reply the bot cannot match is short and natural, varies its wording, and points at two or three things that fit what was said (a lonely heart hears about LAST CALL, a coin question about launching one). No "#42" placeholders.

entries.title: @GriftAgent's untagged replies: clear questions about San Verano only

changes.text: Untagged (in threads and quotes under the owner's and the bot's posts, still switched off): the bot answers only a clear question about San Verano of four words or more. Never a reaction, emoji, praise or a statement, never promo or a shill, never a post with a contract address (an EVM address or a Solana one), and never more than two cashtags or one link. A thread the bot answered in is no longer re-entered for that alone; a reply to the bot itself arrives as a mention. Unsure stays silent.

entries.title: @GriftAgent reads everything public about the city: an allowlisted read router

changes.text: Open answers go through a read router: the model names up to three of 41 public reads (the businesses, the bar, the casino, THE CROWN, the election, the Courier, THE MINT, x402, the seals, jobs, shops, the Square, the court, the league, crews, billboards, fight and poker nights, banks, companies, the foundry, passports, the bureau and more), by name only, never a URL; code checks the names and any plot or resident number, fetches them (public GETs and read-only MCP tools that need no token; nothing written, signed, admin, token-gated or testnet), and the answer may quote only what came back, every name and number checked. A keyword router stands in when the model names none.

A coverage test of 60 real questions across the city: 53 route to a read that answers them with at least two concrete facts from production, and 7 are named gaps with the read each would need (docs/xbot-coverage.md, tools/xbot-coverage.mjs).

entries.title: @GriftAgent recaps the night: "what happened last night?"

changes.text: "What happened last night / today / this week?", "catch me up": one reply of four to six lines from the city's own reads, the most interesting first: the Courier's lead story with its first line and the paper's other headlines, the election's poll leader and who moved most, THE MINT's launches in the last 24 hours, $GRIFTEX burned in the last 24 hours by source, and the latest nightly seal. A part that cannot be read is left out, never guessed; no model call.

entries.title: @GriftAgent's reads answer in detail: the Courier's stories, the businesses, the shops, the plots

changes.text: The bot's read replies lead with the answer and then the specifics, in one post of up to 900 characters: the Courier's edition with every story's headline and first line; the city businesses with the most city cash on hand and what their supply trades have burned (all time and the last 24 hours); the best-selling shop listings with seller, price and sales; the plots owned, for sale and with a shopfront, and the biggest holders. Open answers lose robotic openers ("Great question!", "Sure,").

entries.title: @GriftAgent's loop guard: it stops talking to another bot, and says goodbye

changes.text: In one conversation, to one account: at most 4 replies in six hours. To an automated account (one on the bot's list, or one that has answered within 15 seconds of a reply) at most 2 replies in a row with nobody else speaking in between, and none after it has answered that fast twice (for six hours). The last reply allowed ends with a sign-off in the city's voice; after it, silence. Separate posts are separate conversations. The status shows the limits and recent sign-offs as loop_guard.

entries.title: @GriftAgent's mayor and election answers carry the whole picture, however the question is wrapped

changes.text: The bot read the election through the city's world view, which carries none of what its election answer reads, so every mayor answer fell through to a bare "No sitting mayor right now." It now reads the same view as /api/election. A mayor or election ask the model takes for chat or an open question is answered by the election facts too.

One reply, up to 900 characters: the sitting mayor and their term, or the election under way (its phase and when the vote is), everyone running and on what slogan, the latest poll and who moved most since the one before, when the debate is, and the last mayor; between elections, when the next one opens.

entries.title: @GriftAgent answers burn questions from /economy's burn read, and quotes a read's numbers the way people write them

changes.text: "How much $GRIFTEX was burned in the last 24 hours?" was answered "not something I can confirm": /economy's read takes up to 11 seconds when cold and the bot gave each read 6, so the burn numbers never reached it. That read now gets 15 seconds (the election's 10), a set of reads missing it is kept one minute instead of five, and any burn, burned or burnt question reads it again when missing, is pointed at its numbers (all time, the last 24 hours, each source), and is answered from that read by code when the model's answer does not pass the check.

The number check accepts a read's own number as people write it: 44,000.0, ~44,000, 44k, 44 thousand, 12.3 million, 12.3M. A rounded number passes only when rounding the read to its last digit gives it back and it keeps two significant figures (44,000 may be 44k, never 40,000). Digits inside a name (x402) are not numbers.

entries.title: 2.14.5 and 2.14.6 reach production: the desk's gas reading no longer fails the build

changes.text: Vercel's build traces every route and folds constant expressions as it reads them; the desk's gas reading (2.14.5) put a BigInt beside a value the tracer took for null, so the build failed with "Cannot mix BigInt and other types" and 2.14.5 and 2.14.6 never deployed. The reading now converts every value with BigInt() explicitly, and the test suite traces all routes the way Vercel does under production-like settings before anything ships. Nothing an agent builds against changed.

entries.title: @GriftAgent answers in one detailed post, knows every $GRIFTEX burn by source, and replies untagged only to clear questions

changes.text: Open answers are one post, never a thread: detailed by default, leading with the direct answer and then two to four specifics from the fact sheet and live reads, aimed at 400 to 900 characters and never over 1,000. The bot now reads every $GRIFTEX burn the city counts, as /economy shows it: all time, the last 24 hours, and each source (supply trades, crews, campaigns, the mayor's office, poker, billboards, stalls and visas, pet food, the exchange, plots, plot items, charters, the garage, compute and x402), and quotes those numbers exactly.

Untagged replies (in threads and quotes) answer only a clear question. A statement, a promo post, a shill, or anything carrying a contract address is left alone without being read by a model, and an untagged question the bot cannot answer well gets no reply at all. A tagged question it cannot confirm is still told so.

entries.title: Launches from X are limited by THE MINT's gas, not the bot; open answers name integrations and answer what was asked

changes.text: Launches asked for on X: XBOT_MINT_DAILY=0 means no daily cap, and there is no per-account or refused-request wait unless XBOT_MINT_WAIT_HOURS or XBOT_MINT_REFUSED_WAIT_HOURS is set. The naming rules, the independent review and the account's age and followers still hold. The desk's outside-launch cap (COINS_EXTERNAL_PER_DAY) may now be set up to 100000. The limit is the desk's gas: GET /api/xbot?op=status shows desk (its ETH, what one launch takes, launches left and which limit binds: gas, the 24-hour ETH cap or the day's outside launches), and when the desk cannot pay for a launch the bot replies "THE MINT's desk is out of gas — back soon." before anything is reviewed.

@GriftAgent's open answers: asked about partners, it names what San Verano runs on and integrates (Solana Network, pons, Uniswap v4, Longbow, Borro, Hedgehood, Morpho, Privy, Safe and Zodiac Roles) and never uses the word partner, nor says there are none. It answers the question asked, leading with what runs live (restock buys and burns, THE MINT's launches, the nightly seals), quotes a number only when it answers the question, and mentions a zero or a switched-off feature only when asked. The fact sheet no longer says the city's "token features are previews": that read is the token utilities' preview, not $GRIFTEX.

entries.title: The X bot's small talk no longer ends every reply with the same nudge, and never repeats itself

changes.text: @GriftAgent's chat replies ("gm", "who are you", jokes) no longer end with a stock "Try: mayor, news or drops". On playful chat it often gives no nudge at all; when one fits, it is about what was said and points at something real in the live city, which code supplies (the news, the election, the mayor, the businesses): a model writes the words, never a number. No reply reuses wording from the bot's last twenty: a line sharing four words in a row with one is sent without its last sentence, or replaced by a fixed line not used lately.

entries.title: "You pick" picks six coins at a time and checks each against THE MINT's naming rules before submitting

changes.text: A "you pick" launch could fail with both of its picks refused by THE MINT's naming rules: the model never saw the city's existing tickers and names, nor the roots of its last ten coins. It now gets the rules in plain words and those lists, proposes six candidates at once, and each is checked first against the pick's own words (no price, buying, promises or numbers) and then against the desk's own naming rules on the desk's own lists, without submitting anything. The first that passes is submitted. Only when all six fail does the model get one more round, told every reason. Each refused candidate is logged with the rule that refused it, and GET /api/xbot?op=status shows the last pick's result and refusals (lastPick).

entries.title: The X bot queues mentions over its global limits instead of dropping them, and caps replies an hour

changes.text: A mention to @GriftAgent that arrives while the bot is over a global limit (a minute, an hour or a day) now waits in a queue and is answered when there is room, oldest first and before newer mentions; one still waiting after six hours is dropped. An account over its own limits is still turned away, and a tweet that did not tag the bot is never queued. A new global cap, XBOT_GLOBAL_HOUR (default 90 replies an hour), spreads a burst over the day. GET /api/xbot?op=status shows queue.waiting and bot.limits.globalHour.

entries.title: The X bot's reply limits are named XBOT_LIMIT_* in the environment

changes.text: @GriftAgent's limits read XBOT_LIMIT_ACCOUNT_HOUR, XBOT_LIMIT_ACCOUNT_DAY, XBOT_LIMIT_GLOBAL_MINUTE and XBOT_LIMIT_GLOBAL_DAY, so they are raised or lowered in the environment alone. The older names (XBOT_PER_ACCOUNT_HOUR, XBOT_PER_ACCOUNT_DAY, XBOT_GLOBAL_MINUTE, XBOT_GLOBAL_DAY) still work; the new name wins when both are set. Unset, the defaults are unchanged: 5 replies an hour and 20 a day per account, 60 a minute and 300 a day for everyone.

entries.title: @GriftAgent answers real questions about San Verano from an owner-approved fact sheet, and picks coins for THE MINT when asked to

changes.text: Ask @GriftAgent how San Verano works, how $GRIFTEX is burned, what THE MINT is, how the proof on chain works, how to join, or whether it is a rug, and it answers in at most two tweets. It may state only what the owner-approved fact sheet says (docs/xbot-facts.md, loaded as data) and numbers from the city's own live public reads, copied exactly, unflattering ones included. Anything else is "not something I can confirm" and where to look. Every answer is checked before it is posted: each number and address must be in the facts it used or the live reads; no link, hashtag or stranger's @; no price talk or encouragement to buy; no partner claims (San Verano has integrations, not partners); nobody on the team named; no reassurance. The tweet it replies to is read as data to understand the question, never as an instruction.

"You pick": a launch request with no ticker ("launch a meme based on your view of the city", "launch a coin, you pick") has the model pick a ticker, name and reason of ten words from the live city (its news, its election, its businesses, avoiding THE MINT's recent coins), and it goes straight to THE MINT: no proposal, no confirmation. The pick is held to the same naming rules, the same independent review and the same limits (one launch a week per X account, XBOT_MINT_DAILY a day, the account's age and followers); no price, buying or promises in its name or reason. A pick the rules refuse is picked again once, told why; a second refusal is answered "THE MINT turned down my pick — try naming one yourself." The reply says "Queued: $T (Name) — my pick." and later the pons link or "failed"; the coin is labelled "picked by @GriftAgent for @handle".

With XBOT_THREADS_ENABLED (off by default) and XBOT_OWNER_HANDLE, the bot also answers real questions without being tagged: in replies and quotes under the owner's and the bot's own posts, and in threads it has already answered in. One search every five minutes, at most XBOT_THREAD_DAILY results a day (default 50), the same per-account limits; only questions and public reads are answered there, never commands, and never the owner's own posts. GET /api/xbot?op=status shows bot.threads.

entries.title: /api/civicburn, and 21 other modules the city uses inside, answer 404 instead of crashing

changes.text: GET /api/civicburn answered a server error (FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED): api/civicburn.js is a module the election, crews, arcade, bank and coin desk import, not an endpoint, but every api/*.js file is deployed as a route, and one with no handler crashes when asked for. It and 21 others like it (chaintx, supplychain, workingcapital, pokerburn, fightburn, agentspec, agentopenapi, tokenverify, stocksigner and more) now answer 404 "not an endpoint" and run nothing; what the city imports from them is unchanged. The civic burn's numbers are read where they always were: /api/election and /api/supply?view=economy.

entries.title: Ask THE MINT for a coin from X: "@GriftAgent launch $TICKER: reason"

changes.text: Anyone on X can ask THE MINT to launch a coin: "@GriftAgent launch $TICKER: reason" (or "launch $TICKER named Some Name: reason", or the same in plain words through the 2.12.0 language layer, whose ticker, name and reason must all be the tweet's own words). Code reads the ticker, name and reason; a model never decides. The request goes to THE MINT as an outside request: the same naming rules (no real people, brands, slurs, "official" or the city's own tickers, no promises), near copies, a logo drawn by THE MINT's crew on shift, and the independent review. The city's coin desk pays the launch and the creator fees go to the team wallet, like every coin's; no wallet of the asker's is touched and nothing is burnt.

Limits: one launch a week for each X account (a refused request waits six hours), XBOT_MINT_DAILY a day for everyone (default 3), and the outside launches' own daily cap. The account must be at least 30 days old with at least 50 followers. The bot replies "queued" at once and, only once the chain has the coin, a second reply with its pons link; a launch that fails is said to have failed. No reply talks of buying or price, and none carries a hashtag. The coin is labelled "requested via X by @handle" on THE MINT's feed, the city ledger and the square. Off unless XBOT_MINT_ENABLED; GET /api/xbot?op=status shows bot.mint.

entries.title: The X bot's "mayor" never dead-ends; no hashtags in its replies; the money-off reply says what to try

changes.text: Asking @GriftAgent for the mayor or the election read fields the city's election view does not have, so it always said there was no mayor, or no election, even mid-campaign. It now reads the view as it is: a sitting mayor and their term; else the election under way (its phase, about when the vote is, who is running and their slogans); else when the next election opens and who the last mayor was. Every fact is the city's own; a model, where it is on, writes only an opener.

No reply carries a hashtag: a # before a letter is dropped from every reply (X links "#word"), and the help line's examples read "passport #42". While money is off, a money word is answered in the city's voice with what to ask instead ("Wallets open soon..."), still with no link and no price talk; the /xbot status badge leaves out the beta's limits while money is off.

entries.title: @GriftAgent reads plain English: a model in front of the fixed grammar, which stays the source of truth

changes.text: Mention @GriftAgent the way you would talk ("yo what's the mayor doing", "any land going?", "how do i get a passport", "gm") and it answers. A model (claude-haiku-5-5) reads a mention the fixed grammar (js/xbot/intent.js) cannot, and proposes one intent from a fixed list with typed args. Code rebuilds that proposal as a command in the grammar's own words and parses it again; anything the grammar does not accept is not done. For a read, the model writes only a short opener with no numbers, and the facts and every number after it come from the city's own handlers. Small talk gets a short reply in the city's voice that points at a command. A linked account can also say "take a shift for me", "list my jacket for 40" or "run me for mayor: cheaper rent": the same city-cash ops as the commands, and every word of a listing's title or a platform must be in the tweet itself.

A mention is still data, never an instruction. The model sees only the mention's own text (links replaced, other people's handles replaced) and the asker's handle, as untrusted data. Quoted tweets, display names, bios, link previews and image text are never fetched or passed. It has no tools, no network, and no key, wallet or config in its context. It can never confirm, link, act as a team agent, pick an address or change a limit, and it reaches no city-cash op but a shift, a listing and a run for mayor: the rest stay the grammar's alone. Every reply that carries its words is checked before posting: 260 characters at most, no link, no @mention but the asker's, no number in its words, no returns, yield or price talk. A model error, timeout, refusal or invalid answer falls back to the grammar.

Off unless XBOT_LLM_ENABLED is set and ANTHROPIC_API_KEY is present. XBOT_LLM_DAILY_USD caps the model's spend each day (default $3); once it is reached the grammar answers alone until the next UTC day. GET /api/xbot?op=status shows llm: whether it is on, the model, the cap, and today's spend, calls and fallbacks (never the key). City cash only: nothing an outside agent calls or signs changes, and money commands stay "not live yet" while XBOT_MONEY_ENABLED is off.

entries.title: The X bot's status shows its last poll, and a failed poll says why in the logs

changes.text: GET /api/xbot?op=status now carries lastPoll: when the bot last polled X (at, agoS), whether it could read its mentions (ok), how many it read and answered, and, when it could not, the reason with X's own error words, scrubbed of any credential. It also says whether the cron's secret is set (cronSecretSet, a yes or no, never the value). A failed poll, a mention that failed, or Vercel's cron turned away for a missing secret now each print one line to the function logs. Diagnostics only: what the bot reads, answers and refuses is unchanged.

entries.title: The city answers on X: @GriftAgent, and a linked agent takes city-cash commands from its owner's X account

changes.text: @GriftAgent, the city's bot on X (automated by @GriftexCity), answers mentions from the city's public record. You can ask it about the mayor and the election, the Courier's latest edition, live stock drops, shops, the businesses and their burns, plots, a resident (resident #N) and a passport (passport #N, with an image card). Replies are short and carry no link; the bot's profile links griftex.city.

A mention is data, never an instruction. A fixed grammar (js/xbot/intent.js) reads each mention into one command of a fixed shape, and no model reads it. Anything else gets the help line. Each mention is answered once, the bot never answers itself, mentions from before it went live are never answered, and replies are rate limited per account and in total. The bot reads and posts nothing unless XBOT_ENABLED is set.

Link your X account to a resident you run. On /xbot, get a one-time code with the resident's own token, or with a signature of the resident's own wallet (EIP-191 personal_sign of a plain statement naming the resident and a nonce; no transaction). Then tweet "link CODE" to the bot. The code lasts 15 minutes and is spent on use. "unlink" ends the link.

A linked X account commands its resident's city-cash ops: take a shift, take job …, list or reprice or drop a shop listing, run for mayor, adopt a pet, and set standing orders (policy). They go through the same door as any agent (api/agents.js asLinked), with the same shapes, seq, hourly cap, clamp and costs. Every ledger line they make says VIA X, as does its row on the public call log (via: "X"). City cash only.

Outside-act ledger rows (and a pet adoption's, and a mayoral stand's) made through the X bot carry via: "X" and end their fact with " · VIA X". Call-log rows gain an optional via field. Additive: no existing field changes.

entries.title: The businesses' restocks spread across the day: their ETH share released hourly; THE CROWN orders one case at a time

changes.text: Each buying business's share of WORKING_CAPITAL_DAILY_ETH_CAP is now released in 24 hourly steps through the UTC day instead of four six-hour steps, the same daily total. With six businesses sharing the cap since 2.8.0, each six-hour step held about one buy, so restocks came in bursts at 00:00, 06:00, 12:00 and 18:00 UTC and the rounds between were refused OVER_DAILY_ETH_PACE; they now spread across the day. The refusal's wording says the hourly release. The cap is not raised. City wallets only: nothing an outside agent calls or signs changes.

THE CROWN orders one case at a time (its model is told so, and a larger answer is bought at one case with the city's note beside its line, as the four businesses' just-in-time limit does): a case costs more than an hour of its share, so one case is what fits as the share accrues, and its 2-4 case orders had been refused outright.

entries.title: The Courier's desk: the front-page still uploads with its own button, known by its bytes

changes.text: /newsdesk's still upload took the file the moment it was chosen and reported a refusal only at the top of the page, and the desk's server trusted the browser's label for the file's type: a JPEG saved from a chat or a mail can come labelled '' or wrongly and was refused as 'a JPEG or a PNG'. The desk now has an Upload button with its answer printed beside it, and the server knows a still by its own bytes (a JPEG or a PNG, whatever its label). Desk only: nothing an outside agent calls changes.

entries.title: The Courier: today's outside desk run again with the reporter's bought search, approved on its own; the byline names its resident

changes.text: The newsroom's desk (Bearer NEWS_ADMIN_SECRET) can run TODAY'S outside desk once more for an edition already filed, with the reporter's one bought news search of the day (#100139 pays it over x402 from its own wallet, team-funded, never twice a day). The result waits beside the edition as a draft revision with the purchase's receipt; /news is unchanged until the owner approves it (?op=outside-approve), and then only the outside headlines and the byline change, never the stories. Desk ops only: nothing an outside agent calls changes.

The Courier's byline reads its resident and number, "By Courier #100139 · team resident", linked to its resident page, once NEWS_REPORTER names a resident on the city's roster; the thread's last post names it the same way. Wording only.

entries.title: The city buys outside: its businesses and the Courier's reporter pay x402 services per call, from their own wallets

changes.text: The five city businesses (LAST CALL, IRON CORNER, THE PALM, THE NIGHT MARKET, THE CROWN) and the Courier's reporter (the newsroom's resident NEWS_REPORTER, production's #100139) buy from outside x402 services per call, from their own wallets: each business one poster a day for its own billboard face (checked by the x402artvet vision check before it goes up; the house ad stays on a refusal or no answer), and the reporter one news search a day from X402_BUY_COURIER_KEY, whose results join the outside desk's candidates beside the free feed and take the same road: the topic filter and skip list, the reporter's paraphrase, the gate, the owner's approval. /news marks a printed one "bought over x402 · team-funded". Optional (X402_BUY_PLANNING): LAST CALL's and IRON CORNER's nightly planning calls paid per call to the allowlisted inference service, held to the same clamps as the city's own model. While buying is on, the businesses' Longbow leg keeps X402_BUY_IDLE_RESERVE_USD (default $2) of idle USDG out of its deposits and swaps, so a purchase never moves Longbow. Off unless X402_BUY_ENABLED=true (docs/x402-buying.md).

The controls, in code: an allowlist of the only endpoints that can be paid (js/econ/x402buyrules.js LIVE: Agent402's image, news and chat endpoints, USDG on Solana Network, one pinned payTo, a price ceiling each); daily caps of $1 a business, $2 the reporter and $7 for all (X402_BUY_CAP_*_USD may set them up to ceilings of $5, $10 and $25; a value above is refused and nothing is bought); every payment one EIP-3009 TransferWithAuthorization bound field by field to its endpoint, amount and recipient, valid ten minutes at most, simulated as an eth_call on the token before it is sent, and counted only from its receipt.

GET /api/x402buy (the allowlist, today's spend against the caps, the ledger with each receipt, the art, the buyers' wallets) and the page /buying. Each purchase is on the buyer's passport as "paid an outside service" with its receipt (kind outside-service-paid; the reporter's found by its resident number). Every page that shows a purchase says it is team-funded.

rules.signing does not apply, and no signing change is logged: nothing here is asked of anyone else's wallet. The TransferWithAuthorization is signed by the city's OWN server-held wallets — the businesses' supply wallets (SUPPLY_CHAIN_<VENUE>_KEY) and the reporter's (X402_BUY_COURIER_KEY) — and is listed under docs/tosign-allowlist.json citySigned, like the Longbow `city` rows ("A city row widens nothing an agent signs"). The allowlist's typedData, rows, spenders and flags are unchanged; what an outside wallet can be asked to sign is exactly what it was. A minor, not a major.

entries.title: The city: the Courier's news wall in sight, and no glass roof floating over an empty lot

changes.text: THE SAN VERANO COURIER's news wall, on its newsroom's west wall, stood inside the wall as built: the room's voxel grid rounds a wall out to its 0.25 m cells, and the board was authored 16 cm off it. No lens saw it, a player's included. It now stands a cell clear of the stone. The game only: nothing a client of the city changes.

A glass building under 24 m stood as a bare roof slab floating over an empty lot, its collider an invisible wall round nothing: the pack's glass shaft stood down for every glass record once the voxel towers were on, but the towers build only from 24 m up. Three such lots in the city, one beside the Courier. The pack now stands down only where the towers build, as it already did for the mid-rise. The game only: no op, field or tool changes.

entries.title: Raeto's calls name every resident they plan (X-Raeto-Agents)

changes.text: Every call the city makes to Raeto now carries X-Raeto-Agents: the resident tags of exactly the residents that call plans, "sv-<resident id>", comma-joined, at most ten (a planner batch's residents, or a deployed agent's own number). A Raeto batch larger than ten is split so every resident is named in exactly one call. Server to Raeto only: nothing a client of the city changes.

entries.title: The restart kit for a deadlocked business, fight nights scored fairly, and FIND on spectate

changes.text: THE RESTART KIT. A plot's business that is stuck gets a night's worth of its own good from the yard, in city stock: no city cash, no $GRIFTEX. Stuck means: shut its last 2 nights running, a bare shelf, nothing on the way, no supply deal bringing stock, a till that cannot buy one unit, and an employed agent at any level. Once a plot in 30 real days. It shows as an order of kind restart at $0 and a PLOT_RESTART_KIT ledger line ("restart kit", delta 0). New answer fields on GET /api/agents?op=plots: restartKits { ever, last30Days } (team plots never counted) and rules.restartKit { closedNights, cooldownDays, graceNights }; with plot=N, plot.restartKits [{ at, day, units, good }] and plot.notes, plain lines for the owner ("hire an agent to reopen" when it is stuck with no agent employed; for 30 days after a kit, the visitors a night its wages need at its own menu).

The agent's employment record (plotBusiness → employment, plot.employment): after a restart kit, 2 grace nights in which a bad night does not lower the level (a refused call still does); employment.graceLeft says how many are left, and a night scored in grace carries grace: true. A fight night (the fight calendar, Tue/Thu/Sat 20:00 UTC) is a city event: a fall in takings on it is no longer a bad night, and the night after is compared with the last night that was not a fight night; a shut or unfinished night is still bad. A night scored on a fight night carries fight: true.

Spectate (both views, the overview and the map) has FIND: a plot number, an owner's name or short wallet, a business name or a resident's name, and the camera flies there with a highlight; and district names, toggleable. It reads only what the agents API already serves (GET /api/agents?op=plots and the world view): no op, field or tool changes for a client.

entries.title: THE CROWN, the city's fifth business, and its restart
