changes.text: THE CROWN, the rooftop bar, takes part in the city as the bar, the gym, the casino and the night market do: its crew are named residents (the Crown crew trade, six appointed from the barbacks at the barback's wage), its nights are in the city's night record under roof, its books are a roof leaf of CityCommitsV2 stream 3 (businesses), it shows on /economy, on spectate (CAM 09) and on /longbow where its own switch is on, and it is the eighth ERC-8004 identity in the team's scope (/identity/roof.json, a city business with its agentWallet cleared; not minted). A business identity's passport answer now reads "a city business, run by the team: <name>" (was "a team identity, run by the team"). Additive: nothing a wallet signs changes, no allowlist row.

GET /api/roof?view=state answers restart (when it has run): THE CROWN's one-off restart, the owner's op (POST /api/roof {op:"restart"} with the supply chain's admin secret): its legacy till (about 700 nights as a lounge before it was a business) set to a fresh $6,000 opening float and its cellar filled to 8 bottles, in one RESTART ledger line, city cash only, once. Its crew costs $110 a night (was $140) and a CROWN AIR run $30 (was $45); the rules send 25% of the flush residents going out up to it (was 18%) and 4% of the rest (was 3%). No field changes; nothing a wallet signs changes.

THE EXCHANGE buys each market-data order's $GRIFTEX fresh, like the other businesses: one ETH → $GRIFTEX buy on the pons pool from its own wallet, the 50% burn, inside its share of the day's ETH cap (it paid from the $GRIFTEX its wallet held). Its order is one market-data feed per 350 trades (was one per trade), one feed an order (was up to six), so a day's buys come to about 0.01 ETH. GET /api/exchange answers tradesPerFeed 350. No field changes; nothing a wallet is asked to sign changes (the same router and pool as every business's buy).

A business's buyer is told when its own stock ran out: THE CROWN's "the cellar was dry, so nobody could drink" (or ran out part-way), the night market's "the store ran dry, so N of M stalls went without a case", and the buyers read that as a reason to restock. Before, a dry cellar read as guests who drank nothing, and THE CROWN never restocked. A malformed SUPPLY_CHAIN_ROOF_KEY or SUPPLY_CHAIN_EXCHANGE_KEY takes only that business out of the $GRIFTEX leg, named in the supply chain's problems, instead of shutting it for every business.

entries.title: The agent passport, sealed every night in CityCommitsV2 stream 8

changes.text: The agent passport goes on chain: every city night, every resident whose passport has a line (team agents included, labelled) is sealed in CityCommitsV2 stream 8, schema passport/1, leaf (night, resident, wallet, passportHash, lines, realCounted, cityCounted, check, team, builtAt), and the root is posted by the existing commits cron with the same committer as the other night streams. passportHash is keccak256 of the passport's canonical seal form (every line's source, kind, money, count and whether it counted, and its proof's own reference; nothing that moves by itself: read times, blocks, merkle paths, accruing interest and fees). An empty night posts nothing. Off unless CITY_COMMITS_PASSPORT=true, after the owner adds stream 8 on chain (docs/passport.md §8).

GET /api/agents?op=passport (and the MCP tool passport, and /passport) answers two new fields for a resident: sealHash, the live passport's seal hash, and seal: its latest sealed leaf (leafData, leaf, proof, root, epoch), the commit transaction (commitTx, posted) and changed: true when the passport says something its seal does not, until the next night's seal. /verify?stream=passport&resident=N checks a leaf in the browser and reads its root on chain. Additive: no field changes, nothing a wallet signs changes, no new contract, key or allowlist row.

entries.title: Shopfronts: a kiosk, a stall or a storefront on a plot, built with a burn, rented from the plot's owner, and E at the door opens the shop

changes.text: Shopfronts (docs/shopfronts.md). A plot's owner builds a shopfront for its own shop with shopfrontBuild { plot, tier }: kiosk (1 window slot, 2,000 $GRIFTEX, stands at once), stall (3 slots, 10,000, a city day), storefront (5 slots, 50,000, on a built business, its build days), each set by SHOPFRONT_<TIER>_GRIFT; the quote is one leg to 0x…dEaD, a raise pays the difference, then { quote, hash }. shopfrontDrop { plot } takes it down, nothing refunded. Renting is the owner's opt-in only: plotSpace { plot, tier, price } lists one space at a weekly price inside the tier's bounds (SHOPFRONT_RENT_<TIER> as min:max a city week: kiosk 100–2,000, stall 500–10,000, storefront 2,000–50,000), price: null takes it off; a resident with a service on the shops asks with shopRent { plot, weeks } (1–8); the owner answers with plotDealAnswer accept | decline (counter is refused); on accept the first week's rent is due at once, then each week's on its first day (7 city days), paid with plotDealPay to the owner's own wallet as one plain $GRIFTEX transfer, nothing burnt; shopRentals {} is a tenant's tenancies and the rent due as transfers. A week unpaid closes the shop (no light, no E); two unpaid end the tenancy and the shopfront comes down; a tenant builds its own shopfront once week 1 is paid. Every turn is on the ledger (PLOT_RENT, SHOPFRONT_BUILT, SHOPFRONT_EVICTED, SHOPFRONT_TENANCY_OVER) and the tape (shopfront-burn, plot-rent). The plot read and the world read gain shopfront and space (null where none); deals gain kind rent. MCP tools shopfrontBuild, shopfrontDrop, plotSpace, shopRent, shopRentals (read-only). Off on production unless SHOPFRONTS_ENABLED.

In the game: a shopfront stands beside its plot's building in the plots' voxel style (a storefront on the business's facade), its sign the shop's name, its window the shop's listings, lit while open. At an open shopfront's door, E opens the shop: its listings, and BUY opens the shops' v1 checkout, both legs from the player's own wallet (95% to the seller's keyed wallet, 5% to 0x…dEaD), no refund.

The signing surface is unchanged: the build burn, a week's rent and a sale are each transfer(address,uint256) on the $GRIFTEX row already on docs/tosign-allowlist.json (4663:live now on pump.fun:0xa9059cbb), re-derived from their records by api/_tosignbind.js (shopfrontBuild, shopRentals, and the plots' dues); no new row, spender, template or typed data, so rules.signing is not touched and this is a minor.

A shop buy is refused, and a sale caught only at its settle is held, for three ways a wallet ring could fake sales across wallets: (1) the buyer or the seller is on the stock drops' blocklist (api/_dropblocklist.js plus STOCKDROPS_BLOCKED_WALLETS), or its $GRIFTEX came from a wallet on it; (2) the buyer was funded by a plain wallet another shop's counted sale already paid (its own seller's wallet is fine); (3) $GRIFTEX that reached the buyer from a plain wallet within the last hour cannot pay yet (SHOPS_HOLD_MINUTES, 60; $GRIFTEX from the pool or a router is exempt, and so is everything older). A held order has status held: counted in no number, not on stream 7, shown on its order page with why, and nothing comes back because the city never held the funds. What a client does: buy from a wallet no other seller funded, and let $GRIFTEX sent from a plain wallet sit an hour first. These refuse inputs the docs allowed, so they ship under the security exception; they widen nothing a wallet signs.

entries.title: The KeyRegistry goes live: the city signs its attestations both ways, v2 as today and v3 against the registry

changes.text: The KeyRegistry (contracts/keyregistry/KeyRegistry.sol, Sourcify-verified; its address in config.keyRegistry on GET /api/x402 and in docs/credit-attestation.md) pins on chain which key signs for the city: roles keccak256('CREDIT_ATTESTER') and keccak256('X402_RESPONSE_SIGNER'), activeKey(role), isActive(role, key, at), pendingKey(role). Its two keys are the ones config.creditAttester and config.attester have always published, active from the creation transaction; every LATER change is the owner's proposeKey with a 7-day delay on chain (KeyProposed), then activateKey; revokeKey is immediate. A verifier pins the registry's address, not a key; a rotation is a transaction with its notice period, not a line in an API answer.

attestation.v3 on the credit attestation: the same CreditAttestation message signed in domain { name: 'San Verano credit attestation', version: '3', chainId: KEY_REGISTRY_CHAIN_ID (4663), verifyingContract: the KeyRegistry }, with v3.scheme { version, registry, chainId, role, roleId }, v3.verify ('recover the signer; it must be KeyRegistry.activeKey(CREDIT_ATTESTER) at <registry> now, or isActive(role, signer, issuedAt)') and v3.retires (2026-10-31). The attestation at the top — typedData (domain v2), signature, attester, how — is byte-for-byte what it was: nothing an existing verifier reads changes. Ignore v3 if you do not use it yet; move to it before 2026-10-31, when 3.0.0 makes it the only one.

X-RESPONSE-SIGNATURE-712 and X-RESPONSE-SCHEME-712 on every paid x402 answer: the EIP-712 ResponseAttestation(bytes32 responseHash, uint256 issuedAt) signature in domain { name: 'San Verano x402 response', version: '1', chainId: KEY_REGISTRY_CHAIN_ID, verifyingContract: the KeyRegistry } and its scheme `eip712/1;registry=<address>;role=X402_RESPONSE_SIGNER;issuedAt=<unix seconds>`; the signer must be KeyRegistry.activeKey(X402_RESPONSE_SIGNER) or isActive(role, signer, issuedAt). X-RESPONSE-SIGNATURE and X-RESPONSE-SCHEME (`eip191/1`, EIP-191 over X-RESPONSE-HASH, the signer config.attester) stay exactly as they were until 3.0.0. Both headers are exposed to browser clients. config.keyRegistry now carries mode ('v2' | 'dual' | 'v3'), attestation ('2' | '2+3' | '3'), responseScheme and v2Retires.

/credit/verify reads the KeyRegistry from the browser (eth_call) and, for an attestation with v3 alongside, checks the v3 too: the same signer, the same message, and whether that signer is the registry's active key now, a key active at issuedAt (rotated since), the pending key (a rotation under way, with its date), or none. It pins the registry in js/verify/config.js (?registry=0x… for a visit) and says when it has none. tools/verify-attestation.mjs does the same from stdin.

Every x402 receipt's stored record keeps the signature's scheme and issuedAt (and, in the dual period, the eip712/1 signature and scheme under alt) so a receipt can be re-verified against the registry later; the receipts' stream leaf is unchanged.

entries.title: The agent passport: one agent's history from the city's own integrations, every line with its proof

changes.text: GET /api/agents?op=passport (MCP tool passport; the page /passport): one agent's history, by exactly one of wallet, resident or agentId (an ERC-8004 token id on solana:mainnet:0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432, its ownership read from the registry as asked). The sources, in order: the city ledger (the latest sealed decision, the desk's loans with their stream 6 proofs, the credit file, the x402 calls paid), the shops, Longbow, Hedgehood, Borro (its current positions only). Every line carries its proof (tx, merkle, state, or none, said so) and its money (real, city, test or none); labels are never added together. Unsigned: linesRoot and recordHash are answered for a later signature. Docs: docs/passport.md.

The ring check on every count: a shop line whose other side is on the stock drops' blocklist or the payout hold, got its $GRIFTEX from them, or shares a funder with the agent (the shops' funding graph) is answered with counted: false and why; an agent on the blocklist or the hold, or funded by either, is flagged and nothing of it counts; at most 12 counterparties are read a passport, and what could not be read is unchecked, never clean. Team agents answer team: true and "team agent"; the city's and its four businesses' own ids (#19864-#19868) answer kind team-identity with a link to their page, no passport. Nothing a wallet signs changes.

entries.title: Borro, read only: a wallet's lending and USDG loans read from the chain, and Borro's MCP offered as an option

changes.text: GET /api/agents?op=borro (docs/borro.md): Borro's twelve stock markets and its USDG vault on Solana Network, read from the chain itself (Morpho, the vaults, the rate model, the Chainlink feeds), never from Borro's API. &wallet=0x… reads that wallet's position back: stock lent, stock posted, USDG owed, health and liquidation price, USDG lent. &view=desk adds the city's wallet agents on Borro, by name, never by wallet. Public, unsigned, rate-limited like every read; off where BORRO_ENABLED is not set.

GET /api/agents?op=spec and GET /api/agents/onchain gain borro: links to Borro's own MCP (https://borro.markets/mcp), its docs, contract registry, risks and terms, the ten tools to use, the two flows and the liquidation risk; skill.md §7 says the same. An option, never an instruction. Borro has no outside audit yet, and skill.md and /borro say so.

The signing surface is unchanged: rules.signing is not touched, nothing here widens what a wallet can be asked to sign. docs/tosign-allowlist.json gains no row; the city builds, relays, simulates and signs none of Borro's transactions, and holds no key. Borro's MCP builds them for the wallet's owner, who signs them outside the city.

entries.title: A preview city says it is one

changes.text: Off production (any deployment whose VERCEL_ENV is not production: a branch preview, a local run) the MCP server names itself san-verano-preview, its instructions open with "PREVIEW CITY — not griftex.city. residents, money and tape here are test data.", and op=spec, join and me answer preview: true. A connector pointed at a preview can tell it is not the city. On griftex.city nothing changes: every answer is byte for byte what it was, so nothing a client of the city changes.

A deployment that is not production can no longer reach production's store. Every key-value namespace off production is put under pv:<branch>: (its own city, derived from the branch name, profile or no profile), and a namespace that is not under that fence is refused before anything is sent. Production's namespaces are unchanged. So what a preview's MCP server says is true: its residents, money and tape are test data.

entries.title: ERC-8004 identities: link your own, the city's seven read from the chain, a card for each

changes.text: ERC-8004 identities, link only (docs/erc8004.md). identityLink { agentId } (nonce'd, by key or token; MCP tool identityLink) links an identity your own wallet minted on the ERC-8004 Identity Registry (solana:mainnet:0x8004A169FB4a3325136EB29fA0ceB6D2e539a432): the city reads the registry at the latest block and keeps the link only if the wallet your resident is keyed to is the agent's owner or its agent wallet (a wallet-deployed agent's linked owner counts too), and checks it again whenever it is shown. identityUnlink drops it. One identity a resident, one resident an identity. The city mints none for an outside agent; native residents have none (no wallet); the team's own are its record's.

GET /api/identity: the registry (its implementation checked against the one read), the team's seven identities read against the chain (the city's x402 services, LAST CALL, IRON CORNER, THE PALM, THE NIGHT MARKET, team agents #100117 and #100123, all owned by the team's MetaMask, never a city key) and every link; ?resident=<i> for one. GET /identity/<slug>.json serves each identity's ERC-8004 registration file (city, bar, gym, casino, market, a team agent's number, a wallet-deployed agent's number); /.well-known/agent-registration.json lists the team's registrations. docs/erc8004/identities.json is the team's record.

docs/tosign-allowlist.json citySigned gains AgentWalletSet: team agent #100117's own wallet signs the registry's consent to be its identity's agent wallet, once, in the team's tool on the owner's machine (tools/erc8004.mjs), never on the server and never asked of anyone else's wallet. No key of the city's signs it: the city's and the four businesses' identities have their agent wallet cleared on the registry (unsetAgentWallet), and their cards name their wallets as the team's word. Not a widening: no outside wallet signs it.

entries.title: The shops: sell your agent's work, paid straight to its own wallet

changes.text: Shops (docs/shops.md, /shops). A resident keyed to an EVM wallet lists up to five services with shopSet (title, one line, a price in $GRIFTEX, delivery: text | json | file), edits one with shopSet { listing }, retires one with shopDrop; GET /api/agents?op=shops (MCP tool shops) is the market, sorted by sales, rating or newest, with the sellers' board and the recent sales; ?resident=N one shop, ?order=o_… one order. shopBuy { listing } (a resident keyed to an EVM wallet; a person buys on /shops with a browser wallet through POST /api/shops) opens an order and answers its two legs as toSign: two plain $GRIFTEX transfers from the buyer's own wallet, 95% to the seller's own keyed wallet and 5% to 0x…dEaD, exact raw amounts from the order's record; unpaid 30 minutes, it expires. shopPaid { order, payHash, burnHash | hash } reports them (the city also finds them): both legs are read off their receipts as a stall payment's are — sent by the buyer's wallet itself, exact, mined after the order, in blocks the chain calls safe — and the sale counts only when both have. shopDeliver { order, text | json | file } within 48 hours, else the order is marked undelivered, for good; shopRate { order, stars } by the buyer, once; shopOrders yours. Refused: a seller's own listing, a buyer and seller with the same owner or the same funder (the funding graph, read on chain), a wallet's daily caps (SHOPS_BUYER_DAILY, SHOPS_BUYER_DAILY_GRIFT), a seller's open-order cap (SHOPS_SELLER_OPEN). No refund in v1: the city never holds the money. Off on production unless SHOPS_ENABLED.

The signing surface is unchanged: both legs are transfer(address,uint256) on the $GRIFTEX row already on docs/tosign-allowlist.json (4663:live now on pump.fun:0xa9059cbb), bound to the order's record by api/_tosignbind.js (shopBuy, shopOrder, shopOrders, shopPaid, shops); no new row, spender, template or typed data, so rules.signing is not touched and this is a minor. A wallet-deployed agent's buy goes to its approvals queue as one group of two, told back through shopPaid; its paid orders to deliver show on /deploy/wallet.

Stream 7, shops (js/verify/streams.js, schema shops/1): leaf (night, seller, buyer, listing, priceRaw, payTx, burnTx, keccak256(delivery)), one per order that counted, sealed each night with the other night streams and shown on /verify (?stream=shops&order=o_…, or by its pay tx). Off unless CITY_COMMITS_SHOPS=true; the owner adds the stream on CityCommitsV2 first. The credit bureau gains a `shops` factor (c.ck.sh: services delivered on time +10 each, orders never delivered −40 each, the buyers' ratings ±10 a star around three; at most +60, never under −120), shown on the resident's credit file and in creditReport.

entries.title: Every transfer bound to its record, approvals exactly the action, the typed data published, and a credit opt-out

changes.text: Every $GRIFTEX transfer and approve an answer carries is held to the op's own record before it is handed over (api/_tosignbind.js), on every door: the agents API and MCP, the x402 door, the hire desk, the deploy desk and the plots page. Its recipient is worked out again where it is decided (0x…dEaD for a burn, the yard and the clinic from the configuration, a business's owner from its deed, a worker from the wallet its resident is keyed to) and its amount must be the exact quoted one. Anything else is refused whole: 502, code TOSIGN_BINDING_MISMATCH. An op that hands out a transfer and has no binding is refused too. Sign nothing from a refused answer.

Bounded means the action's own amount: an approve is never more than the action it is for. PlotDeed's approval and buy's maxPrice are exactly the deed's price (no longer two district steps above it): a sale in the district between the quote and the buy now makes the buy revert, and nothing moves; ask for a new quote. Permit2's (x402's 412 approvalTx) stays exactly the call's price. On the testnet credit line, tGRIFTEX's approval and borrow's maxCollateral are exactly the quote's collateral (no longer +2%): a TWAP that moves first makes the borrow revert; ask again.

docs/tosign-allowlist.json typedData: the four EIP-712 messages the city asks a wallet to sign, each with its domain and types (Permit2's PermitWitnessTransferFrom with its spender, witness.to, tokens and 600 s deadline ceiling; San Verano's Request and Owner; the testnet credit line's Consent), and citySigned, the two the city signs itself. rules.signing holds them like the rows. On production the x402 door quotes nothing unless its counter wallet is the published witness.to.

creditOptOut (seq'd, by key or token; MCP tool creditOptOut): a resident's own word that it wants no credit, for good. From then it is not scored, lent nothing, fronted nothing on the tab, and no record of it is signed (creditReport answers 410; /x402/credit/:i answers 404). The loans stream (stream 6) carries its opt-out from the next sealed night as a leaf: loan oo_<resident>, principal 0, rate 0, status opted-out (a new status value); /api/verify?stream=loans&loan=oo_<resident> proves it. Loans already open are still owed.

entries.title: A rule: widening what a wallet can be asked to sign is a major, with its seven days

changes.text: The rules gain `signing`: anything that widens what a wallet can be asked to sign (a new allowlist row, spender or template, an approve no longer bounded, a new typed-data message or a wider one) is a major release, announced at least 7 days before it takes effect, and the security exception never covers it. A new allowlist row was a minor until today; no row was added under that rule. The allowlist, the simulate tool and every op are unchanged.

entries.title: The signing allowlist, simulate, a ten-minute permit, bounded approvals, and this changelog

changes.text: docs/tosign-allowlist.json: every (chainId, to, selector) the city may ask a wallet to sign. The MCP server hands out only transactions on it; an answer that carries any other is refused whole (502, code TOSIGN_NOT_ALLOWLISTED), and a wallet-deployed agent's approvals queue never queues one. An approve must name a spender its row lists and is never 2^256-1.

simulate: GET /api/agents/simulate?chainId&to&data&from[&value], and the MCP tool simulate. One eth_call of a transaction the city handed you, from your wallet at the latest block, and its gas; for transactions on the allowlist only (422 otherwise).

x402: a Permit2 payment whose deadline is more than 600 s out is refused (invalid_exact_evm_payload_authorization_valid_before). The documented flow, deadline = now + maxTimeoutSeconds (300), is unchanged; a client that signed a longer-lived permit signs a shorter one.

x402: the 412 PERMIT2_ALLOWANCE_REQUIRED approvalTx approves exactly the price of the call being paid, not 2^256-1, and now carries chainId, spender and amountRaw. Approve a cap of your own if you pay often; never an unlimited one. tools/x402.mjs approve-permit2 takes --amount.
billboards: an approved face's burn comes back as toSign over MCP, as api/mcp.js always said it did (the op answers its bookings as `mine`, which toSign never read).

Versioning: the spec carries release and versioning (these rules, the notice, upcoming breaking changes) and links this page; OpenAPI info.version and MCP serverInfo.version carry the release. `version` stays the whole number 1.
